narrative:
The 2017 Cleveland Guardians announced themselves immediately, with Francisco Lindor launching a grand slam on April 5th to set the tone for what would become one of the American League's most dominant seasons. April was a winning month, and Michael Brantley's return from injury added another dimension to an offense that would eventually slug 212 home runs. Lindor was everywhere — his bat, his glove, his energy — and the team rode that electricity to a strong start even as May proved slightly uneven, with Cody Allen's bullpen occasionally faltering in high-leverage spots.

The summer months told a story of a team that could not be stopped. June, July, and August saw the Guardians post winning records each month, but the most remarkable chapter was yet to come. Beginning in late August and exploding through September, Cleveland went on a historic tear, going 25-4 in September alone — one of the best single-month records in franchise history. The bullpen's rough patches were overshadowed by an offense that kept finding ways to win, led by Lindor's relentless production and timely contributions from Edwin Encarnacion, Yan Gomes, and Austin Jackson.

The postseason arrived with Cleveland as one of baseball's most feared teams, boasting a 102-win season and a pitching staff anchored by Corey Kluber. Game 1 of the ALDS against the New York Yankees was a rollercoaster — Lindor's grand slam and Jay Bruce's homer gave Cleveland the lead, but a Todd Frazier error situation and late Yankees pressure made it tense. The series ultimately turned on the Yankees' ability to hit even the Guardians' elite bullpen arms, with Greg Bird and Didi Gregorius delivering punishing home runs off Andrew Miller and against Kluber, silencing a Cleveland team that had looked nearly unbeatable just weeks before.

The ALDS exit stung precisely because this team had been so dominant. A 102-win season, a historically great September, and one of the game's best shortstops in Lindor — all of it fell just short of a pennant. The 2017 Guardians will be remembered as a juggernaut undone by October's brutal randomness, a reminder that regular-season brilliance and postseason glory are two entirely different beasts.

chapters.title: Lindor Announces the Season
chapters.description: Francisco Lindor's early grand slam and clutch hits set the tone for a promising April start.

chapters.title: Grinding Through May and June
chapters.description: The Guardians post winning records despite bullpen hiccups and the occasional tough loss in high-leverage moments.

chapters.title: Midsummer Momentum
chapters.description: July brings renewed energy as Lindor and the offense keep delivering while the team racks up wins.

chapters.title: August Wars
chapters.description: A 19-9 August features clutch offensive explosions alongside some of the bullpen's most painful surrendered moments.

chapters.title: The September Surge
chapters.description: Cleveland goes 25-4 in September, one of the most dominant months in franchise history, riding Lindor and a locked-in rotation.

chapters.title: October's Cruel Exit
chapters.description: The Guardians fall to the Yankees in the ALDS despite heroics from Lindor and Bruce, as New York's bats silence a 102-win juggernaut.
